tools.name: reference
tools.description:
What things do, in two books. book="rules" (the default): the rule book of this very game, read once from its
database (mods and DLC included) and cached -- every unit, building, wonder, project, process, promotion, social
policy and ideology tenet, technology, belief, resource, terrain, feature, improvement, specialist and unit
action, with its numbers. book="playbook": how to play through these tools (the turn loop, batches, blockers,
diplomacy, the house rules, the action table). Read-only, usable while it is not my turn. Use it to learn what a
choice means; use state for the live numbers (its chooser rows carry only the enum, the name and live numbers,
never this text) and question for what a popup asks.
`section`: one part per call. Rules sections: terrain, resources, improvements, units, buildings, projects,
processes, promotions, policies, techs, beliefs, specialists, actions; left out, the whole book (tens of
thousands of tokens: read it once at the start of a game if you can hold it, else the section a choice needs).
Playbook topics: start, turn_loop, quiet_turns, batches, verify, blockers, diplomacy, rules, first_turn, orders
(the action table), all; left out, the index of topics with the start section; city_state(s), deals, trade and
league answer with diplomacy.
Returns Markdown. An unknown rules section is refused as {ok: false, err, sections}; an unknown playbook topic
answers with the topic list. Also served as the MCP resources civ5://reference and civ5://reference/{section}.

section.description: one section: a rule-book heading (terrain, units, buildings, ...) or a playbook topic; left out, the book's index
section.title: Section

book.description: 'rules' (default): what everything in this game does; 'playbook': how to play through these tools
book.title: Book

find.description: rules: keep only the headings and the lines containing this word (a section too long for one reply: promotions, buildings)
find.title: Find

annotations.title: The rule book and the playbook

tools.name: turn
tools.description:
The clock: my seat's turn loop, one action per call --
  status: whose turn it is, the `gate` (what must be answered before anything else), what blocks the end. Read-only.
  briefing: my turn in one read -- decisions with their `actions` rows, changes, board, threats, notes. since='previous' (default) or 'turn' (after a context reset); limit rows per list; detail='digest': the event digest alone (no since, no limit).
  finish: run the `actions` rows as a batch, end my turn, wait until it is mine again, return the new turn. A refused row stops the rest and the turn is NOT ended (ended: false, batch.results). notes='new' (default) / 'all': the notebook notes riding on the reply.
  end: end the turn only, no wait.
  wait: block until it is my turn again (the AIs or the other player).
Side effects: finish and end hand the game to the other players and what they do cannot be undone: order and answer everything first; a save (session) is the only way back. Safe to repeat: when it is not my turn, finish only waits, never ends a second turn. One client plays a seat's turn: a second client of the seat is refused with `turn_claim` (args.force=true takes it over). finish autosaves to the quick-save slot (autosave=false skips).
`args`, by name: skip_quiet_turns (keep ending turns, up to N more, while nothing needs me), wake_on (words that stop a quiet run), autosave, force, briefing (the new turn as a briefing). timeout_seconds (finish 600, wait 90): past it, finish and wait answer with the state so far (my_turn false, timed_out true, nothing lost).
Not this tool: what the game asks is question / answer (nothing ends while `gate` is set); the board is state; orders that leave the turn open are batch; saves are session.
Returns the turn: turn, my_turn, `gate`, todo / decisions, digest (what happened meanwhile), notes, at the end game_over with victory / defeat; a refusal {ok: false, err, end_turn: {todo, skip_actions}} names what blocks the turn and the rows that clear it.

actions.description: finish only: order rows to run before the turn ends, [{tool, args}] as the reads hand them back
actions.title: Actions

since.description: briefing: 'previous' (default) compares with my last briefing, 'turn' with the last turn end (after a context reset)
since.title: Since

limit.description: briefing: rows per list of changes and notes (default 8)
limit.title: Limit

notes.description: finish: which notebook notes ride on the reply, 'new' (default) or 'all'
notes.title: Notes

timeout_seconds.description: finish / wait: seconds to wait for my turn before answering with the state so far (default 600)
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

args.description: finish / end only, by name: skip_quiet_turns (a count: keep ending turns, up to N more, while nothing needs you), wake_on (words that stop a quiet run), autosave (default true), force (take the turn over from another client of my seat), briefing (finish: the new turn as a briefing)

tools.name: state
tools.description:
Read the game as my seat sees it: the empire, units, cities, civs and city-states, the map, the league, spies, the screens, and the choices open to me (research, policies, beliefs, trade routes). Read-only, no side effect, usable while it is not my turn. Use it before an order (its rows ARE the orders) and after one to verify; use reference for what things do, question for what a popup asks, turn for the turn's own state.
How to call: `what` names the object, `view` the part of it (left out: the default view), `id` the one object. Objects and their views:
  empire: default, demographics
  notifications: default
  screen: tech_tree, religion, culture, culture_works, great_people, domination, spaceship, wonders, intrigue, trade_routes, deals
  league: default
  spies: default
  units: default, actions
  unit: actions, targets, tactical, home
  cities: default
  city: screen, production, strikes
  map: window, grid, index, frontier
  civs: default
  civ: summary, war, trade_catalog
  city_state: summary, full
  options: research, policies, beliefs, trade_routes, spy_cities
  compare: default
Selectors, by view: x, y, radius for map/window and unit/tactical; mission for unit/targets; kind for options/beliefs and compare; detail ('summary' / 'full') where a view has both; since and limit for lists; item and yield_type for city/production to price one item; `args` for the rest by the old call's name.
Returns: the object as JSON (a list for units, cities, civs; one dict otherwise), with `actions` or `call` rows wherever something can be done: each row is a complete order() call to copy. A wrong `what` or `view` is refused with `choices`, and for an object that takes an id, a `hint` saying where the ids come from (unit ids from units, city-state ids from the `minor: true` rows of civs). Replies are the 1.x reads' replies unchanged.

tools.name: order
tools.description:
An order to something I own: `to` the target kind, `id` which one, `action` the verb, `args` its arguments by name. It changes the game, and most of it cannot be undone (a disbanded unit, a declared war, a purchase). Not a read: state shows the board and hands back the rows, question / answer settle what a popup asks, turn(action='finish') ends the turn. to: actions --
  unit: move, mission, promote, upgrade, disband, trade_route, plunder
  city: produce, purchase, dequeue, sell_building, buy_plot, specialist, work_plot, governor, status, strike, great_work
  empire: research, policy, ideology, switch_ideology, pantheon, religion, enhance_religion, reformation, faith_purchase
  civ: propose_deal, negotiate, peace, demand, friendship, declare_war, denounce, event
  city_state: gift_gold, gift_unit, gift_improvement (or a city-state screen button by its name: pledge, revoke_pledge, bully_gold, bully_unit, declare_war, make_peace)
  league: propose, repeal, vote
  spy: move, coup
How: copy the rows a read hands back (`actions`, `call`) as they are; `id` is a unit, city, civ, city-state or spy id (empire and league take none); `args` holds what the row holds (a plot's x and y, an item's name, a deal's items, an amount). An order runs whole or not at all. `action_id`: a token of mine; a retry with the same one replays the stored reply instead of acting twice.
Returns {ok: true, ...} with what changed (a unit's new plot and moves left, a city's queue, a deal's answer), or {ok: false, err, choices / accepts, example}: the verb is not one of the target's (choices lists them), an argument is missing (accepts names the shape, example a complete call), or the game refuses it (err names the rule, e.g. the unit has no moves, the city is not mine, another client of my seat holds this turn's claim). Nothing is acted on when ok is false.

to.description: the target kind, something I own
to.title: To

action.description: the verb, by target -- unit: move, mission, promote, upgrade, disband, trade_route, plunder; city: produce, purchase, dequeue, sell_building, buy_plot, specialist, work_plot, governor, status, strike, great_work; empire: research, policy, ideology, switch_ideology, pantheon, religion, enhance_religion, reformation, faith_purchase; civ: propose_deal, negotiate, peace, demand, friendship, declare_war, denounce, event; city_state: gift_gold, gift_unit, gift_improvement, or a city-state screen button by its name (pledge, revoke_pledge, bully_gold, bully_unit, declare_war, make_peace); league: propose, repeal, vote; spy: move, coup
action.title: Action

id.description: which unit, city, civ, city-state or spy; empire and league take none
id.title: Id

args.description: the action's arguments by name, as the copied row has them; a refusal shows the shape with an example
args.title: Args

tools.name: question
tools.description:
What the game is asking right now, so answer() can settle it. Read-only; takes nothing. Use it whenever a reply's `gate` is not null or turn(action='status') says discussion_pending; use state for the board and reference for the rules. It shows one of: a decision popup (a tech, a production item, a policy, a promotion, a belief, a ruins reward, a captured city's fate, a Great Person's use, a dig), the leader on screen with their words and the deal on the table, or nothing pending.
Returns the popup's own read -- the question in words plus `answers` rows, each a complete answer() call to copy (the item's name or button number, and the args the popup needs) -- with `gate` on the reply; a leader screen returns the leader, the speech, the buttons and the deal's items; when nothing is asked, {pending: false, decisions: [...]} lists the turn's open decisions instead. Several leaders can queue at a turn start: answering one returns the next under `next`.

tools.name: answer
tools.description: Answer what the game is asking: settle the one popup, leader screen or deal that question() shows, and nothing else. `choice` is the `answers` row's choice: an item's name (a TECH_, UNIT_, BUILDING_, POLICY_, PROMOTION_, BELIEF_ or goody name; liberate / annex / puppet / raze; a dig's choice number), a popup's or leader screen's button number, or on a leader screen accept / refuse (the deal on the table), leave (close it), accept_friendship. `args` carries the rest the popup needs (a promotion's unit_id, a dig's x and y, a stolen tech's player_id, a religion's beliefs and city). Dispatches on the gate: question() shows which question is up and hands back the rows to copy. It acts on the game as the popup's own button would -- an accepted deal, a razed city, a chosen tech cannot be taken back; a choice the popup does not offer, or an answer when nothing is asked, is refused with {ok: false, err, choices} and nothing happens. action_id: a retry with the same token replays the stored reply instead of answering twice. Not this tool: a decision with no popup up (research, production, a policy) is order; what a choice means is reference. Returns {ok, ...} with the popup's outcome and the gate that follows (still_pending and `next` when another leader waits; `next` also names the call that resumes the AIs' round when they are still moving), or the refusal.

choice.description: the `answers` row's choice: an item name, a button number, or accept / refuse / leave / accept_friendship
choice.title: Choice

args.description: what the popup needs beyond the choice: unit_id, x and y, player_id, beliefs, city
args.title: Args

action_id.description: a token of my choosing: a retry with the same action_id replays the stored result
action_id.title: Action Id

tools.name: notebook
tools.description:
My memory, kept beside the game per seat and surviving a context reset or a restart: free-text notes, assignments (what a unit or city is for) and standing orders (a unit's plan the harness carries out one step per turn). Use it for what future-me must know; the game itself holds no plan, and nothing here moves a unit now -- that is order. action, with its args --
  remember {text, tag?, replace_id?}: write a note (returns it with its id; new notes ride on the next briefing / finish); recall {tag?, limit?}: list notes; forget {note_id}: delete a note for good.
  assign {role, purpose, unit_ids? / city_ids?}: give units or cities a purpose that shows in their state rows; assignments: list them; amend {assignment_id, purpose? / role?}; close {assignment_id}.
  give_order {unit_id, steps, interrupt?, purpose?, replace_id?}: steps is a list of at most 6, in order -- {kind: 'move', x, y}, {kind: 'build', build: 'FARM'}, {kind: 'heal', hp: 80}, {kind: 'hold', mission: 'fortify' | 'sleep' | 'alert'} (last) -- run one step per turn at each finish; it never attacks, declares war or ends the turn, and pauses with a reason when a hostile comes near, the unit is hurt or a step is refused; one open order per unit (replace_id replaces it). orders: the plans with their status; cancel_order / resume_order {order_id}.
Not this tool: a one-off move is order(to='unit'); a popup is answer; the board is state. Usable while it is not my turn. Returns {ok: true, ...} with the row written or the rows listed, or {ok: false, err, accepts, example} (an unknown action or a missing argument; nothing is written). A note written on a turn later than the one on screen (a save was loaded) comes back marked later_timeline.

action.description: remember | recall | forget | assign | assignments | amend | close | give_order | orders | cancel_order | resume_order
action.title: Action

args.description: the action's arguments by name: text / tag / replace_id, note_id, role and purpose with unit_ids / city_ids, assignment_id, unit_id and steps, order_id
args.title: Args

action_id.description: a token of my choosing: a retry with the same action_id replays the stored result
action_id.title: Action Id

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Many orders in one call, in order, with the turn left open: actions is a list of {tool, args} rows -- the rows every read hands back (`actions`, `call`): order, answer and notebook rows alike -- each run as that call and answered under `results`. The first refusal stops the rest by default, since the state the later rows were reasoned about is no longer certain (stop_on_refusal=false runs them all); the rows not run come back under `skipped`. force=true takes over this turn's claim when another client of my seat holds it (otherwise the first row is refused with `turn_claim`). Not inside: the turn's wait / finish / end, a load, the seat, the exit, a batch. Each row changes the game as its order would and cannot be undone; a row's own action_id replays. Use it for several orders already decided; use order for one, and turn(action='finish', actions=[...]) when the same rows should end the turn afterwards. Returns {ok, done, results: [one reply per row], skipped?, hint?}: ok is false when any row was refused.

actions.description: the rows to run in order, [{tool, args}], as every read hands them back
actions.title: Actions

stop_on_refusal.description: stop at the first refused row (default true); false runs them all
stop_on_refusal.title: Stop On Refusal

force.description: take over this turn's claim when another client of my seat holds it (default false: the first row is then refused with turn_claim)
force.title: Force

tools.name: session
tools.description:
Saves, loads and the seat of this game session: keep a state before a risky turn, open another save, leave a finished game, say which hotseat seat this server plays. It never plays a turn; use turn for that. Side effects: a load replaces the game on screen for everyone on it, and a hotseat game loads paused until turn(action='wait'); the notebook is per game and seat, so it follows a save of the same game and is not touched by a load. action -- save: a quick save of the game on screen into the one quick-save slot (each finished turn's autosave overwrites that slot, so copy a save you want kept); load {filename}: open that save (a name as the game lists it, without the single/ prefix; the refusal lists the legal ones), replacing the unsaved state, so save first; load_latest: open the newest save, whichever game it is; main_menu: leave the game for the main menu (the game_over gate's way out); seat {seat}: which human seat (0 or 1) this server plays in a hotseat game -- a server pinned with --seat refuses a change onto the other human seat, and never move onto the seat on screen.
Returns {ok: true, saved / loaded, turn, seat, screen} or {ok: false, err} naming why (an unknown filename with the list, a seat that is someone else's, a game operation already running). In a game with other people ask the human before loading.

args.description: load: {filename} (a save's name without the single/ prefix); seat: {seat} (0 or 1)
args.title: Args
